summary: Smilebit and Sega's stylish inline-skating graffiti series, known for cel-shaded city spaces, radio-driven presentation, and music-forward traversal.

entries.title: Jet Set Radio
entries.definitive_edition: Windows HD rerelease where owned, with Dreamcast original as preservation secondary

emulation.emulator: Native Windows plus Flycast/Redream for Dreamcast comparison
emulation.notes: Run the Windows HD build natively where owned; use Dreamcast emulation or hardware to preserve the original release.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows HD rerelease for resolution, Dreamcast original for original-version completeness

primary.why: Jet Set Radio originally released for Dreamcast in 2000, followed by Japanese mobile versions, HD releases on PlayStation 3, Windows, Xbox 360, PlayStation Vita, iOS, and Android, and later storefront delistings on some digital platforms. The Windows HD release is the highest-fidelity native route where owned, but the Dreamcast original remains important for original-release and soundtrack preservation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the owned Windows HD release at the highest stable settings if available; use Dreamcast hardware or accurate Dreamcast emulation for the original soundtrack/version context, and treat mobile routes as historical only.

secondary.why: Preserves the original 2000 release context and soundtrack/presentation that differ from the later HD rerelease.
secondary.how_to_play: Use original Dreamcast hardware with a clean disc/GD-ROM solution or accurate Dreamcast emulation.

entries.remaster_caveats: HD/mobile releases have soundtrack/version differences and some storefront delistings; mobile versions were later delisted because of compatibility issues.

entries.title: Jet Grind Radio

emulation.emulator: mGBA or original Game Boy Advance hardware
emulation.notes: Use accurate GBA emulation or original hardware; link-cable multiplayer requires compatible hardware/emulator support.

primary.why: Jet Grind Radio for Game Boy Advance is a distinct handheld adaptation of Jet Set Radio, developed by Vicarious Visions with an isometric 2D presentation, local multiplayer, and hardware-specific compromises. Game Boy Advance is the only release and therefore the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Boy Advance cartridge on original hardware, compatible handheld hardware, or a high-quality GBA emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a remaster of the Dreamcast game; it is a separate isometric handheld adaptation with reduced soundtrack and altered presentation.

entries.title: Jet Set Radio Future

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox hardware, Xbox 360 backward compatibility, or xemu for preservation testing
emulation.notes: Prefer original Xbox hardware or Xbox 360 backward compatibility for verified play; emulator compatibility should be checked per build.

primary.version: Original Xbox release via Xbox hardware or Xbox 360 backward compatibility
primary.why: Jet Set Radio Future released only for Xbox in 2002, later becoming backward compatible on Xbox 360. The original Xbox release is the complete source version, with Xbox 360 backward compatibility as a convenient access route rather than a separate release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original Xbox disc on Xbox hardware, or on a compatible Xbox 360 using the backward-compatible profile; use original Xbox emulation only where legally and technically appropriate.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or modern rerelease; despite a newer Jet Set Radio project being announced, Jet Set Radio Future remains locked to the original Xbox release family.
